svg.title: Company Rule, Annexation & The 1857 Indian Rebellion (1765–1858)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of the undivided Indian Subcontinent (1765–1858, strictly zero 1947 Partition borders) showing East India Company presidencies, separate British Crown Colony of Ceylon, Bengal handloom deindustrialisation, Lord Dalhousie’s annexations of Jhansi (1854) and Awadh (1856), and the 1857–58 Northern Gangetic Rebellion across Meerut, Mughal Delhi, Cawnpore, Lucknow, Jhansi, and Gwalior.

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: THE SECOND BRITISH EMPIRE (1783–1914)
Company Rule, Annexation & The 1857 Indian Rebellion (1765–1858)
East India Company taxes, handloom ruin, and Lord Dalhousie’s annexations of Jhansi and Awadh fuelled deep anger across northern India.
Sparked at Meerut in May 1857, the uprising shook British power—ending Company rule under the 1858 Act and creating the British Raj.
